quoted_clause: 12,000 × (140/17 + 24.1) GB/token ≈ 388 TB/s — weights per token at B = 17 plus the ≈24.1 GB KV re-read each output token costs
observed: The formula uses 24.1 GB as the KV re-read per output token, but the canonical per-request KV at 9,500 tokens is 24.9 GB (9,500 × 2.62 MB = 24.90 GB). 24.1 GB corresponds to 9,200 tokens (the initial prompt only), not the full 9,500-token context used everywhere else in the chapter.
correction: Replace 24.1 with 24.9 in the formula, update 388 TB/s to ≈398 TB/s, and update '≈14×' to '≈15×'. Alternatively, if 24.1 is intentional (initial-context lower bound), state that explicitly.
acceptance_test: The KV value in the decode-bandwidth formula matches the per-request KV used in the C = 436/24.9037 calculation (24.9 GB), or the text explicitly justifies using a different context length.
verdict_evidence: ch17:125 uses 24.1 in 12,000x(140/17+24.1)=388 TB/s while same bullet uses 24.9 earlier; with 24.9: 397.6 TB/s, 14.8x not 14x.
fix_instruction: Use 24.9 GB: ~398 TB/s and ~15x; or label 24.1 as the 9.2K prompt-only basis.

quoted_clause: under 100% prefix reuse only the final call's new context is prefilled — 11,600 tokens, i.e., 2,400 new tokens (3 × 800 of retrieved context) once the 9,200-token prefix is served from cache
observed: The phrase 'only the final call's new context is prefilled' implies only the fourth model call performs prefill. In fact all four calls contribute: call 1 prefills 9,200 tokens (no cache yet), calls 2–4 each prefill 800 tokens (prefix cached). Total prefill = 9,200 + 3×800 = 11,600 tokens. Additionally, 11,600 includes the 9,200-token cached prefix, so calling it 'new context' is inaccurate — only 2,400 of the 11,600 are new.
correction: Rewrite as: 'under 100% prefix reuse, only the non-cached portion of each call's context is prefilled — 9,200 tokens on the first call (no cache) plus 2,400 tokens of retrieved context across calls 2–4, totaling 11,600 tokens of prefill; the 9,200-token prefix is served from cache after call 1, and the 195 generated γ tokens are already in KV.'
acceptance_test: A reader can reconstruct the per-call prefill breakdown (9,200 / 800 / 800 / 800) from the sentence alone.
verdict_evidence: ch17:257 'only the final call's new context is prefilled - 11,600 tokens'; 11,600 = 9,200+3x800, not final call's context (input 11,795).
fix_instruction: Reword: only non-cached context is prefilled - 9,200 on call 1 plus 3x800 across calls 2-4 (11,600 total).

quoted_clause: serving all 12,000 output tok/s on one host needs 12,000 × (140/17 + 24.1) GB/token ≈ 388 TB/s
observed: The calculation fixes B=17 (KV capacity) while assuming 12,000 output tok/s. At B=17 and ~21 ms/step, the maximum output rate is 17/0.021≈810 tok/s, not 12,000. To serve 12,000 tok/s, the batch would be ~252 at 21 ms/step (or 344 at 8.6 s service), and the weight amortization would be 140/252 or 140/344, not 140/17. The 388 TB/s figure mixes incompatible operating points.
correction: Replace with a consistent calculation: at B=17, max output rate≈810 tok/s, so 12,000 tok/s needs≈15 hosts; or compute bandwidth at the actual batch implied by 12,000 tok/s and the step time. Remove or relabel 388 TB/s as a hypothetical.
acceptance_test: The calculation uses one consistent B, step time, and throughput; max output rate and host count reconcile.
fix_instruction: Recast at one operating point: B=17 ceiling ~810 tok/s => ~15 hosts, or recompute at B~252 (~296 TB/s); use 24.9 consistently.

observed: 'the original conclusion' has no referent in the chapter or in the surrounding text the reader has seen. It reads as an artefact of an earlier draft, and it invites the reader to hunt for a conclusion they have not been given.
